name: application-recurring-rule-builder
title: Recurring Rule Builder
description: Schedule editor for 'repeats every N days/weeks on…' recurrence rules with weekday toggles and an end condition, driven by a typed interval/weekdays/end-mode prop contract.
useWhen: Configuring a recurring event, task, or reminder with an interval, specific weekdays, and an end condition.
Users need to see a plain-language summary of the rule they're building as they edit it.
The recurrence needs to support multiple end conditions: never, a specific date, or after N occurrences.
avoidWhen: The recurrence is a fixed set of presets (daily, weekly, monthly) with no customization — a simple select is simpler than a full rule builder.
You need arbitrary boolean condition logic — use the Query Builder instead, which is built for AND/OR grouping rather than calendar recurrence.
The schedule only ever repeats indefinitely with no weekday or end-date control — a basic interval input suffices.
responsiveBehavior: The interval row and weekday toggle row both wrap via flex-wrap on narrow viewports; the end-condition radio group stacks vertically at any width.
accessibility: Weekday toggle buttons use aria-pressed to reflect selection state, not fill color alone.
The end-condition inputs (date, occurrence count) are disabled via the native disabled attribute when their radio option isn't selected, preventing confusing focus/edit states.
The plain-language summary at the bottom restates the rule in full sentences, giving non-visual users a single place to confirm the configured schedule.

variants.title: Recurring Rule Builder
variants.description: Interval input + unit select, a row of toggleable weekday pills, a three-way end-condition radio group, and a plain-language rule summary.
accessibility: Selected weekday pills use both a filled background and aria-pressed, not fill color alone.

variants.title: Recurring Rule Builder (Dark)
variants.description: Recurring schedule editor adapted for dark surfaces with the same interval, weekday-pill, and end-condition structure.
accessibility: Weekday pill fills, radio labels, and the summary box text must meet WCAG AA contrast on dark surfaces.
